Global Nourish Corp - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Nourish Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a landline, or click the Q&A button in the webcast platform if joining online. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Nourish Corp's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Vargas, Chief Growth Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on seven key areas: impact of new product innovations and launches, overall company performance highlights, impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, EPS guidance and key assumptions, key achievements and challenges in the quarter, gross margin analysis drivers and trends, and capital expenditure plans and priorities.

First, regarding impact of new product innovations and launches: Innovation remains a cornerstone of our Nourish Forward strategy, with us committing about 4.2% of net sales, or roughly $320 million annually, to R&D and technical efforts. In this quarter, products launched in the last 24 months drove an impressive 18% year-over-year revenue boost, adding $420 million to our top line within the overall 12% organic sales rise. This contributed nearly 40 basis points to gross margin growth through premium pricing that's 25-30% above category norms.

Breaking it down by category, our beverages segment, 45% of the portfolio, grew 14% organically. The star was VitaBoost Functional Waters, blending nootropic adaptogens such as ashwagandha and lion's mane mushrooms. It achieved 2.5 times the expected velocity in the first 90 days, reaching 85% all-commodity volume in North American grocery. That line pulled in $180 million in Q3 sales, up 35% from the prior quarter, with 12% household penetration among millennials and Gen Z according to Nielsen. Gross margins hit 52%, 800 basis points better than our traditional sparkling lines, enabled by supply chains using plant-based sweeteners like monk fruit and stevia that slashed sugar by 90%—taste-tested in panels with 1,200 consumers.

In snacks and nutritionals, making up 35% of sales, we rode the protein trend amid GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic cutting impulse snacking by 8-10% per IRI. Our FlexBar Pro bars, packing 20 grams of protein per 100 calories via precision fermentation tech from partners like Perfect Day, rolled out in 15,000 U.S. doors with Walmart and Kroger. They generated $95 million in Q3, up 28% year-over-year, grabbing 4.2 share points in the $12 billion protein bar market. Repeat buys reached 65% by week four via our app, 15 points above average.

Dairy alternatives shone too, with EarthMilk Oat+ Pro—fortified with B12 and D3 through microbial fermentation—up 42% in Europe thanks to Green Deal tailwinds, driving $145 million globally and 22% share gains over players like Oatly.

Regionally, North America at 55% of sales saw 16% growth from innovations countering inflation-weary consumers versus a 3% category drop per IRI. Premium non-alcoholic RTDs like ZenTea kombucha, zero sugar and 50 calories, added 7 share points in convenience stores, buffering a 5% dip in legacy sodas.

APAC grew fastest at 22% organically, powered by localized SpiceRush ready-to-eat curries for India's urban millennials using ghost kitchens for 30% cost savings, contributing $110 million with 40% e-commerce velocity via Flipkart and BigBasket—triple the norm.

In EMEA, sustainability unlocked gains: 75% of new SKUs use mono-material rPET packaging for deposit schemes in France and Germany, yielding 19% uplift despite 12% rises in cocoa and palm oil from West African weather issues.

Backing this is our Agile Innovation Engine, a $150 million AI push with IBM Watson cutting time-to-market from 18 to 9 months via flavor modeling. We've patented 12 new microencapsulation methods for probiotics, lifting NPS by 22 points to 68.

Strategically, with McKinsey forecasting 5-7% CAGR to 2028 driven by innovation, our 2024 pipeline of 25 launches eyes $1.2 billion in FY25 revenue at over 55% margins—like collagen yogurts and upcycled snacks from ADM regenerative ag. We're outpacing peers' moves like PepsiCo's Poppi buy with 30% faster internal speed.

We've hedged 70% of functional ingredients via Chr. Hansen contracts against volatility, and new products' 1,200-basis-point ROIC shows smart allocation. These aren't just add-ons; they form 22% of our $28 billion LTM sales, protecting against U.S. snacking slowdowns.

Second, concerning overall company performance highlights: This was a standout quarter highlighting our portfolio's resilience in beverages, snacks, and nutritionals. Consolidated net revenues hit $15.2 billion, up 8% year-over-year or 6% organically excluding FX and M&A—beating guidance by 150 basis points via 3% volume, 2% pricing, and 1% mix. Pricing held firm as U.S. CPI food-at-home eased to 1.2% YoY per BLS. Power Brands like AquaPure waters, NutriCrunch bars, and ZestEnergy drinks grew 12% organically, now 68% of revenues versus 62% last year, after pruning 15% low-velocity SKUs to redirect $250 million trade spend.

Adjusted EBITDA reached $3.1 billion, up 10%, margins up 90 basis points to 20.4% on 240 basis point gross margin rise to 38.2% from our $500 million ESCO program. ESCO's AI demand sensing with Palantir and IBM Watson lifted forecast accuracy 18% across 250 plants, trimming working capital $400 million YTD. SG&A delevered 120 basis points to 17.8% via zero-based budgeting post-restructuring. Diluted EPS from continuing ops was $1.45, up 12%, with $2.8 billion free cash flow pacing $11 billion yearly, backing our dividend raise to $0.85/share and $3 billion buybacks YTD.

North America, 52% of revenues, jumped 11% organically to $7.9 billion, gaining share across categories per Nielsen/IRI. Premium RTD coffees soared 25%, outperforming amid premiumization.

Third, in terms of impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions: These headwinds dominated, compressing gross margins 210 basis points to 32.4% despite 7.2% constant currency top-line growth. Input inflation was 65% of the drag: snacks/bakery wheat/corn up 28% YoY per USDA from Russia-Ukraine issues; edible oils 22% on palm shortages; cocoa 45% from Ivory Coast shortfalls, hiking cocoa COGS 18%. Dairy milk powder rose 16% on EU energy costs and U.S. avian flu; PET 14%, aluminum 12%; labor up 8.5% U.S., 10% Europe.

North America energy surcharges inflated freight 15%; Europe gas at €250/MWh hit dairy 20%; APAC sugar 19%; LATAM currencies amplified costs 25%. Supply disruptions added 35%: container rates 150% pre-pandemic; U.S. trucking down 10%; Hurricane Idalia hit citrus, monsoons rice. COGS rose 4.5% to $2.8 billion, $120 million one-offs. EBITDA margins fell 140 bps to 18.2%, offset by 9.1% ASP pass-through and $150 million SG&A savings.

Mitigations: 70% hedging wheat/corn at $6.20/bushel saving $80 million, Cargill dairy forwards; diversified palm oil, nearshored 15% beverages to Mexico; SAP IBP AI cut stockouts 25%, turns to 8.2x; blockchain with IBM; plant-based reformulations; Midwest corn mill stake. Inflation eases mid-single Q4, margins to 33.5-34%, baked into guidance with $200 million COGS offset by 8-10% ASP, $250 million productivity—outpacing peers.

Fourth, looking at EPS guidance and key assumptions: For FY2024, we're raising adjusted EPS to $4.55-$4.75, midpoint $4.65, up 10.7% from 2023's $4.20, accelerating prior $4.40-$4.60 on Q3 strength, cost trajectories, international momentum. Revenue 5-7%, organic 4-6%.

Revenue: pricing/mix 2-3%—2-3% NA on RefreshCola Zero/Aquafizz, 4% Europe HFSS; volume/mix 2-3%—1-2% singleserve/RTD, 8% energy from Velocity. NA 3-5%, EMEA 7-9% plant smoothies, EM 8-10%. Gross margins 52.5-53.5% +150 bps: sugar $0.20-0.22/lb hedged 70%, cocoa hedged 60%, SupplySync $250M AI/robotic 100 bps, SKU cull. OpEx 32-33%: SG&A 28-29%, A&P 11% digital, $100M HealthForward R&D, wages 3-4%. Interest $180-200M, tax 22-23%, shares 450M, CapEx $1.2B sustainable/cold-chain.

Assumes CPI 2.5%, functional bev 20% sales +15%, M&A opportunistic. Risks: commodities, sentiment, regs; upside AI pricing.

Fifth, reviewing key achievements and challenges in the quarter: Net revenues $2.85 billion up 7.2% reported, 8.1% organic—4.1% volume, 3.2% pricing, 0.8% mix. EBITDA margins +110 bps to 22.4%, EPS $0.92 up 12%.

Achievements: Non-alc bev 62% revenues +5.3% volume > category 2.1%, Quench Zero +18% velocity 1.2 share, 28% ACV. Snacks NutriBites $120M +9% volume 0.8 share. NA 9.5% organic QSR +12% McD FCB +15%; EMEA 6.2% hydration +22%; APAC 11.4% China e-com +32% India +25%; LATAM 4.8%. AI demand sensing -22% error $45M EBITDA, regen cocoa 20k ha 15% costs, SKU prune 18% +7% basket. Premium 42%, e-com 18%.

Challenges: sugar +28%, cocoa +45% margins -90 bps to 38.2%; APAC freight +$30M, labor idle 1.2 vol; CSD flat, regs/compet -0.5-2 share; FX -1.4%.

Sixth, analyzing gross margin analysis drivers and trends: Q3 at 42.5%, +230 bps YoY/80 sequential—best in 5 years > industry 38-40%, ahead peers. Pricing +300 bps: ASP +5.2% bev 6.1%/snacks 4.8%, premium organic/VitaPlant. Inflation -150 bps: cocoa +22%, dairy +8%, wheat/corn +12%; hedged 70% cocoa $3,200/MT $45M save. Mix +120 bps: premium/health 28% +15% vol plant +22% 48-52% margins. Efficiencies +60 bps: MarginMax 2.1% COGS, AI yield +4%, PET light -1.5%.

Trends: 5Q expansion from 39.8%, freight -15% $12M save. CC 43.1%. NA 44.2% +280, Europe 40.8% +190, APAC 39.5% +150, LATAM 38.2%. Outlook 45%+ : divest low-margin, vertical $150M, Farm-to-Table -12% emissions/15% costs, blockchain 80%.

Seventh, examining capital expenditure plans and priorities: FY2024 CapEx $650M +12% from $580M, from cash flows; cash $1.2B, leverage 1.8x. Mfg 45% $293M, supply/dist 25% $162M, R&D 20% $130M, digital/ESG 10% $65M.

Mfg: $150M automate GA plant 80k/hr VitaQuench +25% throughput -15-18% labor Siemens AI. Supply: $100M hubs Mexico/Netherlands -200-300 bps COGS. NA 50% $325M RTD coffee; APAC 25% $162M Vietnam kombucha; EMEA 15% PET recycle; LATAM 10% cacao. R&D $60M Palo Alto fermentation Perfect Day 5 SKUs +20% margins; ESG $40M solar/water -25% emissions. Intensity to 4.5-5% FY26, ROIC +150 bps 14.5%.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $15.2 billion, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 41.5%, impacted by input cost inflation but bolstered by productivity and mix. Operating income was $2.8 billion, and earnings per share were $1.45. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $4.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for net sales growth of 7-9% and adjusted EPS of $6.20 to $6.50.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Chris Bennett with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

Chris Bennett (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thanks, Chris. As we detailed, input inflation and disruptions were significant, with commodities like wheat up 28%, cocoa 45%, and dairy 16% pressuring margins by 210 basis points. Freight and labor added layers, but our 70% hedging, nearshoring, AI forecasting, and 85% pricing pass-through kept us resilient—outperforming peers with margins recovering toward 34% by year-end.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Hayes with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Laura Hayes (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for new product launches and what is the expected impact?

Tom Vargas (Chief Growth Officer):
Great question, Laura. Our pipeline is robust, with 25 launches targeting $1.2 billion FY25 revenue at 55%+ margins. Building on Q3's $420 million from recent innovations like VitaBoost and FlexBar Pro, which drove 18% uplift and 40 bps margin expansion, we're accelerating in functionals and plant-based—faster than peers, with AI cutting development time and high ROIC.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Torres with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Mike Torres (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Raj Singh (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Mike, we're proactive: diversified suppliers, nearshored production, SAP AI reducing stockouts 25%, blockchain traceability, and hedges covering key inputs. Post-Red Sea and weather events, our hubs and efficiencies cut lead times 40%, turning inventory to 8.2x—positioning for lower COGS amid lingering risks.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Dana Lee with Bank of America. Please proceed.

Dana Lee (Bank of America):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Dana, Q4 organic growth 6-8%, EBITDA margins 23%+, with EPS guide raised on cost moderation, pricing, and innovation momentum. We've embedded mid-single inflation, supply resilience, and regional strength—confident in 10%+ growth trajectory.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in Global Nourish Corp. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
